title: Planar unit-distance conjecture
claim_summary: An OpenAI reasoning model constructed configurations disproving the predicted planar unit-distance asymptotics.

web_search.evidence: The published materials do not fully specify the web-search policy.

environment.human_input: Experts reviewed, contextualized, and later improved/formalized the model proof.

lessons: Cross-domain theorem transfer can be the decisive discovery.
Expert and formal follow-up materially strengthen an autonomous result.

title: Cycle Double Cover conjecture
claim_summary: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra proved that every finite bridgeless loopless multigraph has a cycle double cover.

web_search.evidence: The public prompt permits ordinary mathematical background search but forbids searching for a solution to CDC or merely checking whether it is open.

environment.human_input: Humans wrote the research-manager prompt and audited the resulting proof and formalization.

lessons: Exact completion criteria and explicit rejection of partial reductions matter.
Blind route diversity and dedicated adversarial agents reduce premature convergence.

title: Pairwise-independent correlation-gap conjecture
claim_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro found an explicit five-element coverage-function counterexample to the proposed universal 4/3 bound.

web_search.evidence: The paper gives the exact direct prompt but does not establish the general web-search setting.

environment.human_input: Authors posed the exact conjecture and validated and wrote up the rational certificate.

lessons: Let the model invent a computational representation.
Convert numerical discovery into a compact exact certificate.

title: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR conjecture under dependence
claim_summary: GPT-5.6 Sol Pro constructed a dependent Gaussian factor model whose BH false-discovery rate exceeds the nominal level.

web_search.evidence: The public account says the initial prompt supplied only the definition; it does not establish whether general web access was available.

environment.duration: about 90 minutes for the initial proof
environment.human_input: The author checked the proof and used follow-up turns for simulations, literature, and figures.

lessons: One long coherent run can beat poorly coordinated multi-agent attempts.
Outward-rounded intervals turn asymptotics plus numerics into proof.

title: Farhi-Goldstone-Gutmann QAOA conjecture
claim_summary: Claude Fable 5 completed the missing proof for the depth-p QAOA approximation ratio on the ring of disagrees.

web_search.evidence: The paper documents the formal and numerical loop but not general web access.

environment.human_input: Humans formalized the infrastructure, froze the theorem statement, and audited the accepted proof.

lessons: Freeze the target before model search.
Interleave numerical hypothesis testing with compiler feedback.

title: Deterministic zeroth-order convex-optimization lower bound
claim_summary: GPT-5.6 Sol Pro obtained a near-quadratic lower bound, closing a thirty-year gap up to logarithmic factors.

web_search.evidence: The prompt supplies detailed baselines and traps; independent general web use is not documented.

environment.proof_assistant: Lean for the sharper lower-bound component
environment.human_input: The operator adapted the CDC prompt, supplied the exact oracle model and baselines, and curated/formalized the result.

lessons: Explicitly enumerate model-change and infinite-precision traps.
Freeze a candidate and separate exploration from audit.

title: Gaussian Completely Monotone conjecture
claim_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro found an explicit atomic measure disproving the conjecture and related Gaussian-optimality claims.

web_search.evidence: No original prompt or search policy was located in the paper.

environment.human_input: Human authors verified the construction and supplied the complete proof and certificate code.

lessons: Small atomic measures can expose false continuous inequalities.
Retain exact rational data and rigorous balls.

title: Fisher-information log-convexity conjecture
claim_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro found a two-dimensional hexagonal perturbation counterexample, extended to all dimensions at least two by tensorization.

web_search.evidence: The paper does not publish the original prompt or search configuration.

environment.human_input: Human authors checked, generalized, and wrote up the counterexample.

lessons: Search geometry matched to the symmetry of the functional.
Tensorization can promote a low-dimensional witness.

title: Erdős problem 119
claim_summary: GPT-5.6 Pro and Samuel Korsky proved a lower bound resolving the strongest unit-circle product question.

web_search.evidence: The accepted proof claim does not document web-search use.

environment.human_input: Korsky prompted and prepared the proof; Thomas Bloom and the problem site examined and accepted the claim.

lessons: Attacking the stronger formulation can reveal a simpler route.
Short elementary harmonic analysis replaced a much longer weaker proof.

title: Erdős problem 793
claim_summary: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra derived the exact leading asymptotic for maximal 2-primitive sets.

web_search.evidence: The public announcement and canonical page do not specify web access.

environment.human_input: Przemek Chojecki selected and prompted the problem; the result refines Erdős's 1938 method.

lessons: Refining a known elementary method can expose an exact constant.
Problem selection by a domain expert remains important.

title: Nathanson-Rajagopal sumset-diameter bounds
claim_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro improved exponential diameter bounds to polynomial bounds using h-dissociated sets.

web_search.evidence: Gowers reports short prompts and no serious mathematical input, but does not document a web-search setting.

environment.duration: several runs totaling roughly two hours
environment.human_input: Gowers selected and sequenced the problems; Rajagopal supplied the prior framework and evaluated the new idea.

lessons: A model can contribute a publishable idea inside a strong human framework.
Expert interpretation distinguishes routine tightening from a genuinely new construction.

title: Talagrand convexity problem
claim_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro supplied a key Laguerre-tessellation coupling proposition used in an AI-assisted resolution.

web_search.evidence: A transcript is public but the general web setting is not established.

environment.human_input: Human authors developed the full result; an independent human proof became the main argument and literature supplied related prior machinery.

lessons: Preserve AI-generated lemmas even when a broader human proof supersedes them.
Audit whether a key lemma is already a corollary of recent literature.

title: Grothendieck finite-flat group-scheme question
claim_summary: GPT-5.6 Sol found an order-four counterexample and Claude Fable formalized it in Lean.

web_search.evidence: The workshop account does not specify general search availability.

environment.human_input: Akhil Mathew posed the question; Kevin Buzzard sandboxed, compiled, inspected, and merged the formalization.

lessons: An explicit counterexample plus independent formalizer is a strong pipeline.
Sandbox generated proof code before running it.

title: Jacobian conjecture in dimension three
claim_summary: Claude Fable produced an explicit constant-Jacobian polynomial map over C^3 with multiple preimages.

web_search.evidence: The public announcement gives the formula but not the full prompt or search policy.

environment.human_input: Akhil Mathew suggested the question; Levent Alpoge checked and published the exact object; formalizers encoded it.

lessons: Prefer counterexamples whose validity has a tiny trusted checker.
A finite witness can be stronger evidence than a long model-generated proof.

title: Natural-density logarithmic Collatz descent
claim_summary: AI agents strengthened an almost-all Collatz result to natural density one with explicit logarithmic clocks.

web_search.evidence: The public evidence package does not include a complete web/search transcript.

environment.human_input: Lech Mazur developed and published the mathematical paper and evidence package.

lessons: State scope limits next to the headline.
A density-one logarithmic theorem is not the full Collatz conjecture.

title: ProblemsILike 6 Frobenius-amplitude counterexample
claim_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro and Codex found a characteristic-two Tango-bundle counterexample implicit in the literature.

web_search.evidence: Research and literature retrieval were central; public artifacts include a Codex research log and audit.

environment.human_input: Thomas Bloom and Daniel Litt posed and assessed the problem; humans identified the literature status and checked computations.

lessons: Attention-bottleneck resolutions are valuable but should be labeled.
Record which sources were found and how they imply the target.

title: AlphaProof Nexus formal discovery campaign
claim_summary: A population-based formal prover reported multiple Erdős, OEIS, algebraic-geometry, and optimization results.

web_search.evidence: The documented core loop is formal proof search, not unrestricted browsing.

environment.human_input: Humans selected/formalized the benchmark pool and audited public results; later independent work corrected novelty counts.

lessons: Compiler validation enables evolutionary search over proof sketches.
Formal correctness and novelty remain independent.

title: EinsteinArena verifier-backed records
claim_summary: Agents produced twelve new verifier-accepted records across open optimization and construction problems.

web_search.evidence: The arena API, verifier state, leaderboard, and discussion are documented; unrestricted web search is not a required or established component.

environment.human_input: Humans designed problems and verifiers; agents shared and extended constructions.

lessons: Dense deterministic verifier feedback supports sustained search.
Domain-state access can matter more than general web search.

title: Wang six Erdős proof claims
claim_summary: Shouqiao Wang reported six GPT-5.6 Sol proof claims after long Codex campaigns.

web_search.evidence: The repository contains prompts and artifacts, but web use is not normalized per run in the public claim.

environment.duration: roughly 6 to 32 hours per successful run
environment.proof_assistant: Lean on two of six claimed cases
environment.human_input: Wang selected and filtered the problems, generated exact CDC-style acceptance prompts, funded long runs, and evaluated the artifacts.

lessons: Domain taste and problem selection materially affect yield; the public report was 6 claims from 13 attempts.
Exact completion criteria, route kill conditions, and adversarial repair loops are reusable.
Formal status and public-collaboration provenance must be tracked per problem.

title: Erdős problem 421 gap-greedy claim
claim_summary: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra proposed a density-one gap-greedy construction with distinct interval products.

web_search.evidence: The public proof claim does not document web or tool use.

environment.human_input: Przemek Chojecki is credited for the construction; Rob Sneiderman submitted the proof claim for independent checking.

lessons: A complete-looking claim remains provisional until independent checking.
Keep operator and submitter attribution distinct.

title: Two-dimensional Gaussian Moments Conjecture candidate
claim_summary: A 24-minute GPT-5.6 run proposed a structural and p-adic proof of GMC(2).

web_search.evidence: The public shared chat does not establish the web-search setting.

environment.human_input: A human supplied a short either-counterexample-or-identity prompt; later checking is primarily by other models.

lessons: A sophisticated proof draft is not independently verified evidence.
Cross-model agreement should trigger, not replace, formal or expert audit.

title: Knuth TAOCP Fascicle 8A Exercise 210 candidate counterexample
claim_summary: GPT-5.5 Pro produced a finite counterexample to a knight-tour denominator claim.

web_search.evidence: The author publishes the prompt and code but does not establish general web access.

specialized_tools: independent code execution by two coding agents
environment.human_input: The author selected the exercise, used a public prompt template, and published the code while explicitly requesting expert review.

lessons: Executable finite claims are easier to audit than long prose proofs.
Independent implementation remains preferable to re-running the same source.
